chunks: Safwān ibn Mihrān al-Jammāl narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:

A man from the hypocrites died, and al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام went out walking. He met a mawla of his and said to him, 'Where are you going?' He said, 'I am fleeing from the جنازة of this hypocrite lest I should pray over him.' So al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام said to him, 'Stand by my side, and whatever you hear me say, then say the like of it.'

He said: then he raised his hands and said, 'O Allah, disgrace Your servant among Your servants and in Your lands. O Allah, make him enter the most intense of Your Fire. O Allah, make him taste the heat of Your punishment, for he used to be loyal to Your enemies, show enmity to Your friends, and hate the Ahl al-Bayt of Your Prophet.'

key_terms.أَخْزِ: disgrace or abase; a supplication for humiliation
key_terms.أَشَدَّ نَارِكَ: the fiercest of Your Fire; an expression of severe punishment
key_terms.أَهْلَ بَيْتِ: the Household; the family of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءَكَ: Your friends or loyal servants; those devoted to Allah
key_terms.الْمُنَافِقِينَ: the hypocrites; those marked by hypocrisy in faith

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام say at the funeral of a hypocrite?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts that Imam al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام attended the funeral context of a hypocrite and taught a companion to repeat a supplication condemning the deceased for allegiance to the enemies of Allah and hostility toward His awliya'. It highlights disavowal from hypocrisy and enmity toward the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام, while also preserving a historical report connected to funeral prayer.
